hpi: {{patient_name}} is an older man with chronic osteoarthritis who presents with epigastric abdominal pain of one week's duration. History reveals extensive, prolonged use of oral ibuprofen for knee pain. NSAIDs block both COX-1 and COX-2, impairing gastric prostaglandin production and disrupting mucosal defense — this is classic NSAID-induced gastropathy. Symptoms began one week ago and the patient is medically stable. Conservative management is key: discontinue NSAIDs, start a proton-pump inhibitor, and follow up in 2-4 weeks. If no improvement with conservative therapy, then EGD would be indicated, but ordering it now loses points — the USMLE tests restraint from invasive testing. H. pylori should be ruled out. For his osteoarthritis, switch to acetaminophen and/or topical diclofenac gel rather than oral NSAIDs. Address modifiable risk factors: smoking cessation and alcohol avoidance.
